newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil edges up, supply good.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil edges up, supply good.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil rose a little on Thursday after crude's recent strong rally but traders said high storage levels in ARA and good supply coming into the region left little room for strong gains.
High sulphur barges traded at $98 fob ARA, and at $97.50 for a small piece loading this month. The offer for early Febwas then pegged at $98. Storage tanks in ARA are relatively full.
High sulphur cargoes were a little stronger, too. An oil major was heard bidding for barrels at around $97 cif NWE, but a regular buyer said he had heard talk a dollar or two higher than that.
A broker said a 120,000 tonne cargo of transatlantic fuel oil was due to discharge in ARA next week, and at least one more Venezuelan is due to arrive in ARA in the same time period.

Russian cargoes added weight to Europe's supply. The consultancy Petrologistics said on Thursday that total fuel oil exports from the Black Sea and Baltics was 160,000 tonnes in the third week of January, compared to 250,000 tonnes in the second.
Low sulphur fuel oil was steady to firmer. On Wednesday a U.K. utility was heard to have bought a cargo, with relatively poor quality specifications, from a U.K. refiner at $110.50 cif U.K.
